extraction.name: VQAonline
extraction.description: VQAonline is the first Visual Question Answering (VQA) dataset in which all contents originate from an authentic use case. Sourced from the online question answering platform Stack Exchange, it contains 64,696 visual questions with images, natural language questions, context, and accepted answers validated by the individual asking the question. Answers tend to be much longer (mean of 173 words) than in prior VQA datasets. The dataset spans 105 diverse topics across five super-categories: culture & recreation, life & arts, science, professional, and business.
extraction.creator: Chongyan Chen, Mengchen Liu, Noel Codella, Yunsheng Li, Lu Yuan, Danna Gurari
extraction.publisher: University of Texas at Austin; Microsoft; University of Colorado Boulder
extraction.inLanguage: Multilingual (primarily English, also includes Germanic, Romance, East Asian languages, and Russian)
extraction.citeAs: Chen, C., Liu, M., Codella, N., Li, Y., Yuan, L., & Gurari, D. (2024). Fully Authentic Visual Question Answering Dataset from Online Communities. arXiv:2311.15562v4
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created by scraping data from the online question-answering platform Stack Exchange. The publicly-available data spanned from August 2010 to November 2022. Data was collected from 105 topical sites. Each example required four components: a natural language question, a natural language context, an image, and at least one answer marked as 'accepted answer' by the questioner.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Visual questions without an accepted answer were removed (reducing from 330,705 to 165,766). Visual questions with scores of 0 or less for either question or answer were removed. Visual questions with multiple images or visual answers were excluded. Examples where images could not be downloaded from the provided link were also removed.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Stack Exchange archive hosted at https://archive.org/details/stackexchange in XML format, covering 105 topical sites across five super-categories (culture & recreation, life & arts, science, professional, business). 75 technology topics (e.g., Stack Overflow, LaTeX) were excluded.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Starting with 330,705 candidate visual questions: (1) removed visual questions without an accepted answer (resulting in 165,766); (2) removed visual questions with scores of 0 or less for either question or answer (resulting in 119,177); (3) removed visual questions with multiple images (resulting in 85,573); (4) removed visual questions with visual answers (resulting in 65,849); (5) removed examples where the image could not be downloaded (final dataset of 64,696). All images were converted to png format for consistency. Dataset splits: 665 training, 285 validation, 63,746 test examples.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For user intention annotations, three crowdworkers from Amazon Mechanical Turk were hired. Workers were given instructions, taxonomy definitions, and two examples per user intention category. The interface showed the question, context, and answer. Workers A and B independently labeled one primary user intention per visual question. When annotations disagreed, worker C broke the tie by selecting between the two provided options. For human evaluation of model performance, ten domain experts (each with at least a Master's degree in the relevant field) rated model-generated answers on a three-point scale: incorrect (0), partially correct (0.5), or correct (1).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk for user intention annotations; home-grown web-based interface for domain expert evaluations (code available at https://github.com/VQAonline/VQAonlineVisualization)
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The user intention taxonomy was refined through four rounds of annotator analysis on 105 visual questions. Agreement accuracy improved from 53.3% to 87.5% and Cohen's kappa agreement improved from 45.24% to 84.69% across rounds. For model answer evaluations, 1200 human judgments were collected for 200 VQAs. Pearson correlations between human judgments and evaluation metrics were calculated: LLaMA2 (0.975), METEOR (0.971), BERTscore (0.900), RefCLIP-S (0.892), ROUGEL (0.874), CLIP-S (0.662).
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: For user intention annotations: 2 annotators per VQA, with a 3rd annotator for tie-breaking when disagreement occurred. For domain expert model evaluation: 1 domain expert rating per VQA for each of 6 model-generated answers.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Crowdworkers for user intention annotations: located in the United States, completed more than 500 HITs with over 95% approval rating. Domain experts for model evaluation: 10 individuals located in the United States, each a domain expert in one of 10 topics (Physical Fitness, Botany, Music, Mechanics, Politics, Law, Chinese Language, Economics, Statistics, Artificial Intelligence) with at least a Master's degree in the related field.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-3.5 (used for initial bootstrapping of user intention taxonomy); DeepSolo (state-of-the-art text spotter model used to detect text in images); LLaMA2 (used as an evaluation metric).
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Dataset is publicly shared at https://vqaonline.github.io/
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset includes user-generated content from Stack Exchange users. The paper notes the dataset may include multilingual content reflecting users from various countries.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The authors expect improved models designed for VQAonline can benefit real-world applications including community question answering platforms (e.g., Yahoo! Answers, Wiki Answers, Quora), learning assistance VQA tools for children, virtual assistants, visual dialog and query, as well as visual search and browsing.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may poorly represent people in poverty-stricken areas since VQAs are posted by Stack Exchange users with access to mobile devices and Internet. The geographic representation of Stack Exchange is unbalanced, with more contributions from countries like US, India, Europe and fewer from countries like Egypt. The dataset has language imbalance with performance discrepancies across languages (best for Germanic Languages, followed by Romance Languages, then East Asian Languages, and Russian). The dataset exhibits a long-tail distribution across topics (from 10 to over 20,000 examples per topic).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset may poorly represent people in poverty-stricken areas and has unbalanced geographic representation. The answers in the dataset are notably long (mean 173 words), making the standard VQA evaluation metric ineffective. Models trained on Stack Exchange data (including BLIP2, MiniGPT-4, LLaVA, mPLUG-Owl, InstructBLIP, GPT-4V) may have unfair advantages when evaluated on this dataset. The dataset exhibits a long-tail distribution across topics.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, and testing for Visual Question Answering models, particularly those supporting long-form answers. Supports few-shot learning with splits of 665 training, 285 validation, and 63,746 test examples. Used for benchmarking VLMs including BLIP-2, MiniGPT-4, LLaVA, mPLUG-Owl, InstructBLIP, and GPT-4V. Also useful for research on multilingual VQA, text VQA, and long-form text evaluation metrics.
